stem: What is the **systems development life cycle**?

options.content: The series of stages followed to develop a new information system
options.rationale: Correct: from problem identification through to maintenance.

options.content: The time a computer takes to start up and load its operating system
options.rationale: That is the boot process.

options.content: The number of years a computer lasts before it must be replaced
options.rationale: That is the hardware's lifespan.

options.content: The steps the processor takes to fetch and execute an instruction
options.rationale: That is the fetch-execute cycle.

explanation: The SDLC is the ordered set of stages used to develop or replace an information system.

stem: Which fact-finding method involves the analyst **watching** staff using the current system?

options.rationale: Correct: the analyst watches the system in use.
A questionnaire collects written answers.
An interview is a conversation.
Record inspection examines documents.

explanation: Observation means watching the current system being used.

stem: In which stage of the SDLC are users trained and the old system replaced by the new one?

options.rationale: Analysis studies the current system and requirements.
Correct: installation, data conversion, training and changeover happen here.
Design plans inputs, outputs, files and processes.
This decides whether the project is worthwhile.

explanation: Implementation includes installing the system, converting data, training users and changing over.

stem: An analyst needs the views of 1,500 customers spread across Zimbabwe. Which fact-finding method is most suitable?

options.rationale: Interviewing 1,500 people would take far too long.
Observation shows actions, not customers' views.
Correct: it reaches many people cheaply and quickly.
Documents do not hold customers' opinions.

stem: Which is an **advantage** of an interview over a questionnaire?

options.content: Many people can be asked in a short time
options.rationale: This is an advantage of a questionnaire.

options.content: The analyst can ask follow-up questions to get more detail
options.rationale: Correct: interviews are flexible and detailed.

options.content: The answers can be completely anonymous, so people answer more honestly
options.rationale: Interviews are face to face, so they are not anonymous.

options.content: It costs less of the analyst's working time
options.rationale: Interviews take more of the analyst's time.

explanation: Interviews allow questions to be explained and followed up, giving detailed answers.

stem: An analyst wants to know which fields appear on a clinic's patient admission card and how many cards are completed each week. Which method should she use?

options.rationale: Staff opinions will not reliably give the fields and numbers.
An interview gives views, not the actual document layout.
Watching staff for a day may not show weekly volumes.
Correct: examining the cards shows the fields and the volume.

explanation: Record inspection gives the actual data, fields and volumes used by the current system.
hints: Which method shows the actual fields and volumes of data?

stem: Which is a **disadvantage** of observation as a fact-finding method?

options.content: It cannot show how long each task actually takes
options.rationale: Observation is good at showing timings.

options.content: Only written answers to set questions are collected
options.rationale: That describes a questionnaire.

options.content: Staff may work differently because they know they are being watched
options.rationale: Correct: behaviour can change under observation.

options.content: Documents that the analyst reads may be out of date or incomplete
options.rationale: That is a disadvantage of record inspection.

explanation: When staff know they are observed they may follow procedures more carefully than usual, so the analyst may not see the real system.
hints: What happens when people know they are watched?

stem: A school asks whether it can afford a new library system, whether its staff could use it and whether suitable hardware exists. Which stage of the SDLC is this?

options.rationale: Analysis studies the current system in detail after the go-ahead.
Evaluation reviews the system after it is in use.
Correct: it decides whether the project is possible and worthwhile.
Design plans the new system's inputs, outputs and files.

explanation: Questions of cost, technical possibility and users' ability are technical, economic and operational feasibility.
hints: Which stage decides whether to go ahead at all?

stem: Questionnaires allow the analyst to ask follow-up questions when an answer is unclear.
explanation: False. Once a questionnaire is handed out, unclear answers cannot be followed up. Interviews allow follow-up questions.

stem: The SDLC is called a cycle because evaluation and maintenance can reveal new problems that start the process again.
explanation: True. As needs change, a system eventually needs replacing and the cycle restarts.

stem: Match each activity to the SDLC stage in which it takes place.

left.content: Data flow diagrams of the current system are drawn
Input screens and report layouts are planned
The program is tested with normal, abnormal and extreme data
Users are asked whether the system meets its objectives

explanation: DFDs: analysis. Screen and report layouts: design. Testing: development and testing. Checking objectives: evaluation.

stem: Match each situation to the most suitable fact-finding method.

left.content: Getting the detailed requirements of the managing director
Finding out what 800 learners think of the tuck shop
Checking whether clerks really follow the official procedure
Finding the fields used on existing invoices

explanation: Detail from one key person: interview. Many people: questionnaire. Real behaviour: observation. Existing data: record inspection.
hints: Many people → questionnaire; actual data → records; what really happens → observation.

stem: Complete the order of the SDLC stages.

payload.template: 1 Problem identification, 2 {{blank:a}}, 3 Analysis, 4 {{blank:b}}, 5 Development and testing, 6 {{blank:c}}, 7 Evaluation, 8 Maintenance

explanation: In order: Problem identification, Feasibility study, Analysis, Design, Development and testing, Implementation, Evaluation, Maintenance (documentation is produced throughout).
hints: The cycle begins with the problem and ends with keeping the system running.

stem: State the job title of the person who studies an existing system and designs a new one.
explanation: A systems analyst investigates the current system and designs the new one.

stem: Describe what happens during the problem identification (preliminary investigation) stage.

points.description: The problems with the current system are identified / defined
The objectives of the new system are set
The scope is agreed / a short report decides whether a full feasibility study is worthwhile

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The analyst briefly studies the current system to find out what is going wrong, sets the objectives the new system must meet, agrees what is in and out of scope, and reports whether a full feasibility study should go ahead.

explanation: The preliminary investigation defines the problem, sets objectives and scope, and reports whether to continue.
hints: What does the analyst write in the first short report?

stem: Compare interviews and questionnaires as methods of fact-finding. Give **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of each.

points.description: Interview advantage: detailed answers / follow-up questions / body language
Interview disadvantage: time-consuming / few people / not anonymous / expensive
Questionnaire advantage: many people quickly and cheaply / anonymous / easy to analyse
Questionnaire disadvantage: low return rate / cannot follow up / misunderstood questions

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An interview lets the analyst ask follow-up questions for detail, but it takes a long time so only a few people can be interviewed. A questionnaire reaches many people quickly and cheaply, but questions cannot be explained and many forms may not be returned.

explanation: Interviews give depth from a few people; questionnaires give breadth from many.
hints: One advantage and one disadvantage of each method.

stem: Mutare Valley Clinic (fictional) records patient visits on paper cards. Cards are often lost and patients wait a long time. The clinic has 12 staff and about 4,000 registered patients. Nyasha, a systems analyst, is asked to investigate.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which SDLC stage is Nyasha starting?

options.rationale: That is when the new system is installed.
That follows implementation.
Design comes after analysis.
Correct: she is investigating what is wrong.

parts.explanation: Investigating the problems is the first stage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Match each group to the most suitable fact-finding method.
parts.explanation: One key person: interview. Many patients: questionnaire. Existing cards: record inspection.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Nyasha also decides to observe the reception desk. Give **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of this.

points.description: Advantage: sees what really happens / where delays occur, first-hand
Disadvantage: staff may behave differently when watched / time-consuming / problems may not occur that day

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: She can see for herself where patients wait and why cards go missing, but the receptionists may work more carefully than usual while being watched.

explanation: (a) Problem identification. (b) Interview, questionnaire, record inspection.
hints: Think about how many people and what you need to know.
The cycle starts with the problem.

stem: A school in Bulawayo is replacing its manual fees system with a computerised one.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each activity to its SDLC stage.

left.content: The bursar is trained to use the new system
The fees screen layout is planned
Errors found after six months are corrected

parts.explanation: Training: implementation. Screen layout: design. Fixing errors later: maintenance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The analyst wants the views of all 900 parents. Recommend a fact-finding method and justify your choice.

points.description: Justification: many parents can be reached quickly and cheaply / they can answer in their own time / anonymity

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A questionnaire, because 900 parents are too many to interview and a questionnaire can reach them all quickly and cheaply, letting them answer at home.

hints: Each stage has its own activities.
Justify the method with the size of the group.
